comment: Every dashboard route (archive/MY_MORNING_NEWS_PLAN.md section 25.4, plus the sign-in and account routes of section 33.1) mapped to a mobile screen. Status: implemented (the screen exists and works against the server today), planned (the screen or its scaffold exists, and the named plan phase delivers the server routes it needs), or not-applicable (operator and administrator pages that stay on the web, with a reason). Screen paths are relative to src/. npm run parity:check enforces this; npm run parity:strict (before store submission) also fails on planned.

routes.notes: Server URL with Change server, email, password, optional tenant, tenant picker for contract B.

Shown only when client config has signupEnabled (sign-in hides Create account otherwise). Email, password (8 or more characters), name, optional promotional code (filled from /signup?code=), the terms and privacy links, and the age box from minimumAge, then Check your email with Send a new link (or Your account is ready when verification is off). When client config carries a turnstileSiteKey the app has no WebView for the check, so it opens the web sign-up page instead.

Opened by the emailed /verify?token= link (universal link, src/lib/deepLinks.js). Confirms once, then offers Sign in; a link that does not work offers Send a new link. Sign-in also offers a new link on 403 EmailNotVerified.
Linked from sign-in. Warns when client config has emailEnabled false, since the link cannot be sent.
Opened by the emailed /reset-password?token= link. New password with confirmation, then Sign in; signs this device out when the reset account is the one signed in. A rejected link offers a new one.

Today merges the dashboard Home and Today pages. At a glance shows the overview tiles for the last 30 days (runs with completed and failed, findings shown and rated, relevance precision, prediction accuracy with resolved and open, and feedback with how much carried a reason) and links to Insights; it stays out of the way on a server without the overview. Recent topic run briefings stand in for the runs panel. Keep-or-delete prompts for topics that found nothing new for a week sit at the top (Keep, Delete with a confirmation, Open topic), followed by a dismissible card that offers notifications for new briefings: Turn on asks for permission, registers this device, and turns on briefing pushes for an account whose Phone choices are all off; Not now is remembered on the device.

The latest ready edition briefing, Compose now with status polling until the briefing is ready, recent topic run briefings, and the one-time request entry point. Audio and per-item feedback live in the briefing reader.

List with status and deliverables; detail (today/requests/[requestId].jsx) with the plan, clarifying questions, plan again, confirm now or at a time, cancel, make recurring, open the report, and delete. Polls while scheduled or running. Tablets show the detail beside the list.
Text, deliverables, length, run now or once at (device time zone), recipients, podcast feed, and Just do it. A 502 ModelError keeps the saved request and offers to open it.

Recurring topics with status and last run; tablets show the workspace beside the list. Duplicate, delete, and bulk actions stay on the web. Keep-or-delete prompts for stale topics sit above the list, which reloads after a Keep or Delete.

Compact wizard: Describe, Dimensions (weights, lock, add, remove, regenerate with guidance), Questions (every kind, skip, ask more), Brief (edit, draft, constraints), Review (create or abandon). Each model step degrades to a manual path on 502 ModelError. Feed and seed-page suggestions and the preview run stay on the web; schedules are set in the workspace.
The same screen resumes a session (?session=) or finds the topic's active session (?topicId=) and offers Refine again.

Workspace tabs on mobile: Overview (Run now, dry run, pause or resume, refine, brief, dimensions, constraints), Findings, Runs, Sources, and Schedule (every interval type: weekly, every N days, weeks, hours, or minutes, days of the month, once, cron, manual, with an optional start and end, the missed-run policy, a next-run preview, and the switch that makes audio automatically for every run briefing). Feedback, preferences, analytics, and per-topic prompts and models join with Phase 10 or stay on the web. Overview shows the topic’s own keep-or-delete prompt; after a Delete the workspace says the topic is gone. Overview > Compare with past briefings (also in the wizard): mode, issue count, start date, pinned issue, and context budget, with Preview the baseline for the values on screen (issues, size against the budget, truncation, note, and the 400 and 409 answers inline) before Save.
Runs live in the topic workspace Runs tab on mobile, refreshing while a run is queued or running.

Status, totals (duration, findings, duplicates, sources, queries, tokens, cost), the stage list with a hand-rolled SVG duration chart, result dispositions, queries, and the run's findings. Polls while active and offers Cancel. Retry from stage stays on the web.

Ranked across topics with tier and minimum score filters, Pinned only (pinned=true), and Show hidden (includeHidden=true); also per topic in the workspace. Rows show Pinned and Hidden badges. Each row has inline rating chips with the current rating (one feedback read per list) and a More button whose menu pins or unpins, hides or unhides, and deletes after a second tap to confirm; the change applies to the list at once (on tablets also from the detail beside it).

Tier, score, Pinned and Hidden badges, why it matters, the score breakdown (SVG bars), and the verified evidence quotes, each with Open the source for its link (the detail carries the source, so GET /v1.0/api/evidence/{id} is not needed). Pin or Unpin, Hide or Unhide (a hidden finding says it is left out of lists, briefings, and emails), and Delete after a second tap to confirm (then back to the list). Relevant, Somewhat, or Not relevant with the current rating selected, and the why sheet (reason, change, retract), on channel Mobile.
Sources live in the topic workspace Sources tab on mobile (title, domain, date, times seen; tap to open). Rating and blocking domains arrive with Phase 10 feedback.
Due to grade (horizon passed or a proposed resolution), open, proposed, resolved, and all, with inline Accurate, Partially, Inaccurate, and Too early ratings.
Statement, confidence, horizon, rationale, the pipeline's proposed resolutions with Accept and Reject, grading with a note, and the accuracy rating with the why sheet.
By status, with Accept, Done, Snooze (1 day, 1 week, 1 month), Dismiss, and Reopen inline, and Useful or Not useful with a reason.
Every briefing, newest first, filtered by editions, topic runs, one-time, or pinned. Tablets show the reader beside the list.

The reader renders Markdown with native components (no WebView or HTML), with section navigation, citation numbers that jump to Sources, linked items with inline ratings on findings, pin, share or save the .md and .html files, and regenerate expired files. Audio: Make audio (409 AudioInProgress, AudioDisabled, BriefingNotReady explained; hidden when client config has audioEnabled false), progress while it is made, Listen streamed from the artifact with the bearer token and Range, Download for offline use with chapters, the chapter list with seek, and the section being read marked in the text. Feedback on the briefing with the why sheet. Compared with: a collapsible card from the comparison read with the summary sentence, the baseline issues (tap opens that briefing), and the changes labeled New, Changed, Correction, Resolved, Unchanged, or Unavailable (tap opens the finding or prediction it names), "No material changes found", and a plain note for standalone briefings. Hidden on a server without the route.

List and edit (topics/editions/[editionId].jsx): settings, topics in order (none means all active topics), schedule, Compose now with polling, and Preview. Creating and duplicating editions and choosing templates and voices stay on the web. The edition also has its own comparison settings with the baseline preview (Off keeps the topics' own comparisons) and System briefings in this edition: subscribed publications in order (at most 20), unavailable ones marked until removed, and 402 CapReached explained. The section is hidden on a server without the publications route. The picker reads the edition detail's publications array, falling back to the paged GET /v1.0/api/editions/{id}/publications; POST /v1.0/api/editions/{id}/publications/enumerate is not needed (at most 20 entries fit on one page). The subscriptions to choose from come from GET /v1.0/api/catalog?subscribed=true sorted by title, 25 per page with Load more and a server-side search box; saved and chosen picks stay listed when they are not on a loaded page.

Ready episodes newest first (tap to play with chapters, or open the briefing), the full player (listen/player.jsx), downloads with offline playback and storage management (listen/downloads.jsx), and a link to the podcast feeds. Background audio and lock-screen controls through expo-audio.

routes.reason: Template authoring (Markdown editor with live preview, validation markers, version diff, import and export of .md files) needs a large screen and a keyboard; it stays on the web dashboard.
Template authoring stays on the web dashboard (see /templates); briefings composed from templates are read in the app.

routes.notes: Precision, coverage, shown, and rated tiles; precision over time (chart 6) and by topic, tier, dimension, and source domain (charts 9 and 10) as react-native-svg charts; evidence quality (verified quote share by model, chart 29); 30, 90, or 365 days. Weight tuning proposals stay on the web.

Accuracy rate, mean Brier, agreement with the agent, due, open, resolved, and time to resolve tiles; the calibration reliability diagram (chart 15) with each bucket in words; accuracy by topic; a link to grade due predictions.

Volume, reasons, and email link tiles; feedback per day, by channel (chart 11; Dashboard, Email, This app, API, and MCP client), and by target; reason themes; suggestion outcomes (chart 19); and the history filtered by target type with edit (reason in place, or a new rating), retract, and open the item.
Proposed first, filtered by status; accept, reject, disable, enable, edit, delete; write your own with a kind and an optional topic.
Members see their own usage (cost, calls, tokens, by task or model) with react-native-svg bar charts; also under Account. Cost by user and CSV export are administrator views and stay on the web.

Model endpoints and assignments are operator configuration; operator and administrator pages stay on the web (plan section 35.3).

Prompt editing is operator configuration that stays on the web (see /prompts).
Search provider setup is operator configuration that stays on the web.

MCP server registration and tool toggles are operator configuration that stays on the web.
Text-to-speech voice setup is operator configuration that stays on the web; the app plays the audio it produces.
The email outbox (resend, delete, send test) is an operator page that stays on the web; members manage their own email preferences under Account.
Request history is an administrator diagnostics page that stays on the web (plan section 35.3).
The API Explorer is a developer tool that stays on the web (plan section 35.3).
Worker, queue, and provider health is an operator page that stays on the web; the app shows the server version under About.
Security audit events are an administrator page that stays on the web (plan section 35.3).
Tenant management is a global administrator page that stays on the web (plan section 35.3).
User management is an administrator page that stays on the web (plan section 35.3).
API credential management is an administrator page that stays on the web (plan section 35.3).
Role management is an administrator page that stays on the web (plan section 35.3).
Role assignment is an administrator page that stays on the web (plan section 35.3).
Server settings and restart are operator tasks that stay on the web (plan section 35.3).

routes.notes: About shows the app and server versions, copyright, and legal links; Account > Server shows the address and changes it.

Profile, password, language, theme, and app lock, plus Plan and codes (account/plan.jsx: the effective plan, its limits, end date, and what starts later, and Redeem a code with friendly text for every PromoCodeInvalid reason; account/redeem.jsx opens from mymorningnews://redeem?code=), Notifications (account/notifications.jsx: a row per kind with Email, Phone, and In-app switches, the address email goes to, devices, and per-topic unsubscribes; turning on a Phone switch asks for permission, saves the preference, then registers the device; account/email.jsx opens the same screen; the in-app list is today/notifications.jsx behind the bell in the Today header), and Podcast feeds (account/podcast.jsx: create for all editions or one, the URL once with Copy, Share, and Open in Podcasts, revoke, delete revoked; hidden when audio is off). Topics that keep running (account/slots.jsx, plan section 8.4): the custom topics in keep order with Move up and Move down buttons that announce the new position, which ones run under the plan limit, the limit and over-limit explanation (from the summary route), Save, and Clear. The editor reads the whole order by walking the pages of GET /v1.0/api/account/topic-slots/topics (1000 per page) and reads it again after Save or Clear, which return the summary only. Plan and codes shows the entry when the account has custom topics and a finite limit, and the Topics list shows a banner that opens it while topics are past the limit.

Required by both stores. Optional password, type DELETE to confirm, then sign out; signing in again during the 7-day grace period cancels it. Links to the web deletion page as well, and falls back to it on a server without the route.
Downloads the ZIP with the bearer token and opens the share sheet.
Browse, subscribe, delivery preferences, suspended access, shared issues and private listening progress.

The system briefing issue reader, also opened by the links in an edition's From your system briefings section (src/lib/deepLinks.js maps /dashboard/catalog/{publicationId}/issues/{issueId}). It shows the issue, shared audio, and the same Compared with card from the issue's comparison field; baseline taps open the other issue of the same publication.

Native purchase/restore controls require build 7 and configured approved store products. A captured signup discount never becomes a full-price store purchase: US App Store users get a web checkout button, US Google Play users get a text notice, and other storefronts get a neutral notice (APP_STORE_SUBMISSION.md section 3.1). Store validation remains a release gate.
Private keys, validation, explicit BYOK selection and repair.
